newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end higher, eyes on Clariant.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end higher, eyes on Clariant.

text.p: Swiss shares ended higher, moving in a tight range following early gains but under the psychologically important level of 3,900 points in the Swiss Market Index (SMI) they had seemed ready to tackle at midday.

Dealers said the market concentrated on chemicals maker Clariant, which jumped 13 percent after Germany's Hoechst announced it would merge its speciality chemicals business with Clariant and take a sizeable minority stake in Clariant.
One dealer said the move was surprising and positive for the market. "Swiss shares are still good for surprises", he added.
The SMI ended up 11.4 points, or 0.29 percent, to 3,885.4.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was up 7.77 points, or 0.31 percent, to 2,481.74 points.
Traders said there was strong buying interest from abroad. Sentiment was expected to remain favourable.
Clariant shot up 13.39 percent, or 60 francs, to 508 francs. Other major pharmaceuticals also saw heavy volumes.
Roche certificates, which led the active list, gave up most early gains to close five francs higher at 10,080. Sandoz climbed 1.25 percent to 1,535 francs.
Monday's star performer Electrowatt slid four francs to 507.

Financials were mixed. Speculation of a possible Swiss interest rate cut were dismissed as unlikely after first giving shares some support in early trade, one trader said. CS Holding, UBS and insurer Zurich lost between 0.5 and 0.8 percent. Insurer Baloise continued a recent rise, adding 1.55 percent to 2,945.
Industrials profited from the easing tendency in the Swiss franc. Alusuisse, Surveillance and SMH firmed more than one percent each. Second-tier Fischer, Siegfried and SEZ posted bigger gains.
Stocks of high tech group Esec gave up four percent.
